function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine plus points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” policy for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right yields.
• Stop signs require a full stop; yield signs require yielding to traffic already in the intersection.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can lead to traffic citations and liability in accidents. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Drivers must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus’s stop sign is retracted. | Violations can result in a $200 fine and points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Drivers must signal before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Improper lane changes can lead to citations. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only in fog or heavy rain. | Failure to use headlights can result in a $50 fine. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, driveways, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Parking violations can be ticketed or towed. | | **Points System & License Suspension** | • Texas uses a points system: 4 points for a first offense, 6 for a second, 8 for a third.
• Accumulating 12 points within 2 years leads to license suspension. | Points are removed after 2 years of no violations. | | **Commercial Vehicle Rules** | • Commercial drivers must adhere to Hours‑of‑Service (HOS) regulations.
• Additional licensing (CDL) required for certain vehicle types. | Violations can lead to fines and CDL suspension. | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Texas uses automated speed cameras and red‑light cameras in some counties. | Violations are mailed to the registered owner. | | **Emergency Vehicle Exemptions** | • Drivers may exceed speed limits and ignore stop signs when pulling over an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. | Must still exercise caution and yield to the emergency vehicle. | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)**: Official rules and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code**: Legal text for all traffic laws. - **Local County Websites**: Some counties have additional ordinances (e.g., speed limits, parking restrictions). ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they override general rules. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your local county’s website** for specific speed limits or parking rules. 4. **Keep your driver's license and registration current** to avoid penalties. If you need more detailed information on a specific aspect (e.g., DUI penalties, school bus rules, or commercial driving regulations), let me know!
